text:
eva_support: FYI customer (acct ACME) reports random tool outputs mapped to the wrong tool when they call two tools in parallel. Happens intermittently, ~1/200 calls.

sam_engineer: can you paste the original request payload and a failing response?

eva_support: here's a sanitized snippet from the customer (they included router_id and correlation headers). They say tool_a result shows up under tool_b in the `tool_results` array.

`POST /v1/call-tools`
```
{
  "request_id": "req-8743",
  "correlation_id": "corr-ACME-42",
  "tools": ["search", "calculator"],
  "parallel": true,
  "args": { ... }
}
```

failing response (trimmed):
```
{
  "request_id": "req-8743",
  "tool_results": [
    { "tool": "search", "result": { /* calculator answer */ } },
    { "tool": "calculator", "result": { /* search hits */ } }
  ]
}
```

maria_oncall: thanks. any correlation_id differences in logs? if correlation id at runtime is per-subcall maybe getting reused incorrectly.

ryan_eng_runtime: that sounds like an association bug in the fanout layer; we had a recent change that pooled worker connections and reused a per-request context header for performance. tagging @alex_sre for SRE watch.

alex_sre: looking at infra logs now. I see multiple entries with the same x-redwood-call-id across different child requests:
```
[2026-02-10T14:02:11Z] call_id=req-8743 child_id=0 x-redwood-call-id=call-984
[2026-02-10T14:02:11Z] call_id=req-8743 child_id=1 x-redwood-call-id=call-984
```
that should be unique per child.

sam_engineer: exact reproduction steps requested. eva, can you ask the customer for a curl with verbose headers? also capture a base64 dump of the response they saw.

eva_support: asked, customer provided one more example and a small log sample, same pattern. They also included a fast repro script:
```
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call-tools -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"tools":["search","calculator"],"parallel":true}'
done
```
They say failure rate ~0.5% with parallel=true, 0% with parallel=false. :thinking_face:

ryan_eng_runtime: ok that's a smoking gun. probable root: when multiple child tool calls are dispatched in parallel we reuse a completion callback that appends results into a shared array without tagging by unique child id. race condition. I can reproduce locally with a loop at high concurrency.

sam_engineer: can you paste the failing stacktrace/log lines?

ryan_eng_runtime: here's the minimal trace:
```
runtime/fanout.go:217 append(resultArray, childResult) // missing per-child slot assignment
runtime/handler.go:89 dispatchToWorker -> reuses callCtx.RequestID
```

maria_oncall: severity? customer is impacted in production but low frequency. Should we create an incident and offer credits?

eva_support: customer asked for credits and a P0 investigation. they already escalated to their engineering lead.

alex_sre: create incident, tag eng-runtime, and set page to oncall. I'll enable a temporary mitigation: flip the `parallel` flag on incoming requests for that org at the proxy to force sequential execution until patch.

sam_engineer: patch plan: (1) add per-child sequence index and preallocate result slots to maintain ordering, (2) ensure call-id header is generated per-child not per-request, (3) add unit tests that spawn 1000 concurrent fanouts and assert tool->result mapping. I'll cut a hotfix branch and roll to canary.

ryan_eng_runtime: will do. quick fix candidate: in fanout dispatcher set `x-redwood-child-id` before dispatch and use it to place result. pushing a patch to hotfix/fanout-assoc-2101 now.

deploy_bot: deploy queued: hotfix/fanout-assoc-2101 -> staging (job 6782).

sam_engineer: also add correlation logging to include the original index and tool name so we can trace back. once staging looks good, schedule canary to a small % of traffic for 30m.

alex_sre: mitigation applied at proxy for org ACME. rolling back the proxy rule will unblock when canary passes.

maria_oncall: customers impacted: ACME; tier: enterprise; escalate billing team to prepare credits if rollback doesn't fully resolve.

billing_bot: Noted. Draft credit: 10% monthly usage for affected window. Please confirm incident and exact timeframe.

sam_engineer: ETA for patch verification?

ryan_eng_runtime: staging tests pass; canary scheduled in 10m. I'll post results.

(10 minutes later)

ryan_eng_runtime: canary OK after 30m, no mis-associations in ~200k requests. rolling to 25% -> monitor.

alex_sre: proxy mitigation removed for ACME.

eva_support: customer confirmed they no longer see the failure in their next batch. they asked for root cause summary and timeline.

sam_engineer: drafting RCA: root cause race in fanout result aggregation caused by reusing per-request context for per-child work; fix: per-child IDs and preallocated result buckets; deployed hotfix and rolled out via canary, mitigation at proxy for affected orgs.

maria_oncall: closing page if no regressions after 24h. good work team :thumbsup:

sam_engineer: also added e2e test to CI to prevent regressions.

eva_support: sending final summary + credit note to the customer now.

deploy_bot: deploy completed: hotfix/fanout-assoc-2101 -> prod (job 6782), rollout 100% success.

ryan_eng_runtime: follow-up: I'll open an issue to audit other pooled contexts for similar reuse.

eva_support: thanks all, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
